title: Base change preserves stable labelled pointed curves
statement: Let $f:W\to T$ and $a:T^{\prime}\to T$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $n\in\mathbf N$ and let $s_i:T\to W$ be labelled sections, with $fs_i=\operatorname{id}_T$. Suppose $(f,(s_i))$ is a stable pointed curve in the precise normalized-component convention [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]. Then $W\times_T T^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}$ [def-pc-fibre-product], equipped with the labelled sections $(s_i a,\operatorname{id}_{T^{\prime}})$ and their projection identities, is a stable pointed curve in the same convention. No Noetherian, nonempty-base, smooth-family, or nonzero-number-of-markings hypothesis is imposed; the family has no prescribed total genus.

source.place: section-stable-curves and lemma-stable-curves (base-change meaning of the moduli stack); labelled convention and expanded proof from StablePointedModuliGroupoids.pullback_properties, de Jong (1997), section 3.6, and Pikaart--de Jong (1995), section 2.3.3.

proof.text: Unpack stability. Projectivity survives by isProjectiveBundle_pullback_snd. Flatness and local finite presentation survive by Mathlib morphism-property base change. Fix the resulting local-finite-presentation witness for the nodal-fibre predicate.

For every algebraically closed field Omega and b:Spec Omega -> T-prime, paste pullback squares to identify the new geometric fibre with W times_T Spec Omega for the composite b followed by a. The comparison is an isomorphism over Spec Omega. Transport connectedness, topological dimension, reducedness, pure dimension, and the completed nodal local-ring isomorphisms. Smooth loci are identified because the isomorphism is over Omega.

The section projection equation gives disjointness of the new section ranges from disjointness of the old ranges. Smoothness along each new marking follows by base change of the smooth open around the corresponding old marking. This preserves labels, including an empty label set.

The fibre isomorphism bijects irreducible components and identifies their reduced normalizations by the universal properties of reduction and normalization. It is over Omega and identifies the preimages of the nonsmooth locus and each labelled section. Hence normalized-component genera agree (pullback of the structure sheaf along an isomorphism preserves ordinary H dimensions), and so do the encard values of special-point sets. Transfer the bounds for genus-zero and genus-one components and assemble the stability conjunction. Empty bases are covered by the universal geometric-point quantifier.

proof_origin.note: Expands the existing pullback_properties docstring into the explicit transport argument; source places are given in the statement and proof.

mathlib_searches.results: Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry has no IsStablePointedCurve. The project defines it in StablePointedCurve; its occurrences elsewhere are hypotheses or conclusions, not this theorem.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No duplicate; SemistableMarkedBaseChange uses a different multipointed-pair predicate and does not provide normalized-component stability.

lean.statement:
theorem isStablePointedCurve_baseChange {W T T' : Scheme.{u}} (f : W ⟶ T) {n : ℕ}
    (s : Fin n → (T ⟶ W)) (hs : ∀ i, s i ≫ f = 𝟙 T)
    (h : IsStablePointedCurve f s hs) (a : T' ⟶ T) :
    IsStablePointedCurve (pullback.snd f a)
      (fun i ↦ f.baseChangeSection (s i) (hs i) a)
      (fun i ↦ f.baseChangeSection_snd (s i) (hs i) a)
